source: WHO/AASLD 2024 Guidelines for the Prevention, Care and Treatment of Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection
recommendations: Initiate antiviral therapy with high barrier to resistance (e.g., tenofovir or entecavir)
Educate patient on treatment adherence, side effects, and risk of transmission
Screen family members and sexual partners; recommend HBV vaccination if susceptible
Assess for advanced liver disease or cirrhosis before starting therapy

follow_up.action: Initiate antiviral therapy and perform baseline renal function checks
Monitor serum creatinine, eGFR (especially if on Tenofovir), and ALT levels
Monitor HBV DNA levels, ALT, and perform ultrasound screening for HCC if high risk

contraindications.action: Avoid TDF; use Tenofovir Alafenamide (TAF) or Entecavir instead

emergency_signs: Acute liver failure: rapid onset of jaundice, coagulopathy (easy bruising), altered mental status (hepatic encephalopathy)
references: WHO Guidelines for the Prevention, Care and Treatment of Persons with Chronic Hepatitis B Infection, 2024
